3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the petitioner was arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 26.11.2025.
Further, the petitioners property worth Rs.2 Crores has been attached.
Hence, she prayed that the petitioner may be released on bail.

4. The learned Government Advocate (Criminal Side) would submit that there is already three cases pending against the petitioner the offences are grave in nature and the investigation is at initial stage and hence he strongly opposed to grant bail to the petitioner.
5. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
